h: Making a Watford Day of It
p: The big plus with this branch is that you don't need a car to get the most out of it. Watford Junction has fast trains to and from London Euston, and it's a straightforward walk or a short bus ride into the town centre, so families coming out of the capital can make a proper outing of it without battling the M25.

That central spot means everything else is close by. The Harlequin, now known as atria watford, has plenty of places for lunch, and the Palace Theatre on Clarendon Road puts on plays and a much-loved family panto at Christmas if you fancy a bit of culture after all that bouncing.

Got a Harry Potter fan in the house? The Warner Bros. Studio Tour London is out at Leavesden on the edge of Watford, where the films were made. It's a big, long visit and tickets must be booked in advance, so it's one to plan for separately rather than squeeze in after a session. Still, pairing the two across a weekend makes for a very happy child.

For the trampolines themselves, the usual rules apply. Turn up with comfy clothes on, empty pockets, and allow a bit of time to sort everyone out before your slot starts. Younger children often do better on quieter weekday sessions, while older kids tend to like the buzz of a busier weekend.

If the sun comes out afterwards, Whippendell Woods on the far side of Cassiobury Park has bluebells in spring and plenty of trails to explore. It's a proper bit of countryside right on the edge of town, and a nice reminder that Watford is more than shops and the M1. Pack a picnic in the car and you've got the second half of the day sorted for next to nothing.
